relevance_note: This review of A20 haploinsufficiency in East Asia states "A total of 74 patients in 39 families were affected by HA20 in East Asia" and gives individual-level facts (age, sex, symptoms, treatment) for three named-in-text HA20 patients.
method_note: Review article; no per-patient table and no per-patient reference column, so source_reference_in_review was left 'not reported' for the three people I could describe. Only three in-scope people have individual-level detail: all are mentioned in the Discussion. Two of them are said to have received allogeneic HCT for HA20 ("allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) was also performed for one refractory patient in East Asia and one refractory patient in other regions (31, 47)"): the 14-year-old English boy (refs 31/47) and the 6-year-old Japanese boy (refs 31/47); the paper calls these the first and second case of allogeneic HCT. I recorded a third person, "a patient who received autologous HCT because of central nervous system vasculitis" (ref 30). Three further people are mentioned only as single counts with one fact each and were not given rows, because the scope rule asks for an individual-level fact beyond the diagnosis: "One patient with HA20 in East Asia developed Hodgkin lymphoma (10)", "only one patient in East Asia showed elevated ISG expression (47)", and "Only one patient was treated with anti-IL-1 agents (canakinumab) in East Asia (47)"; the last two may well be the same person as one of the two HCT cases, and the paper never links them. Table 1 ("The comparison of symptoms and treatment between East Asia versus other countries") contains only group counts (n/total patients) with no patient identifiers, so it yields no person and no per-person feature; the two cells of Table 1 that list diseases separated by commas are group lists, not cells of stacked per-patient values. Contradiction found: the text says the age of onset "ranged from neonatal to around 30 years in both groups", while Table 1 gives "neonatal period to 32 y" for East Asia and "2 mo to 29 y" for other regions. I used no positional reading of any stacked cell. Checklist: I marked type 1 diabetes observed for the English boy because the paper says he developed "insulin-dependent DM" (DM is defined in the Table 1 notes as diabetes mellitus) and skin lesions observed for the Japanese boy because "psoriasis" is listed among his features. For the English boy the paper mentions "hepatitis", "enteropathy" and "cell depletion", but because 'autoimmune hepatitis' and 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' are narrower than the paper's words, and 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' is broader than 'enteropathy' (and 'bowel disease' is not named for him), I left those three checklist items not reported and said so here. The single symptom "frequent fever" of the Japanese boy does not exclude 'recurrent fever', so that item is not reported. Other judgement calls: the ages '14-year-old' and '6-year-old' are the only ages printed for these two boys and are not said to be onset ages, so I recorded them as age at last evaluation (and left onset and age at diagnosis not reported); the English boy is not East Asian and so is not part of the 74 counted in cohort_size_as_stated, which I read as the East Asian cohort only ("A total of 74 patients in 39 families were affected by HA20 in East Asia"). HPO candidates are suggestions with null IDs, since I would not risk an ID. No variant rows were emitted: no TNFAIP3 variant is tied to any identifiable person in this paper.
